notes.title: Ura missions and visual updates
notes.content:
[p][b]Hi everyone,[/b]
[/p][p]For the last month, I’ve been focusing on various game improvements coming from both your feedback and internal goals. I’d like to share the highlights of this patch as well as include a full change log. If there’s anything you think is missing in this patch or should be added to future ones, please let me know![/p][p][/p][p][b]Game difficulty and balance[/b][/p][p]As you might have noticed, the game can get very tough quite quickly, even on lower difficulties. My goal is to create a game that’s easy to pick up, but hard to master. A game that both new and experienced strategy fans can enjoy.[/p][p]Therefore, I’ve made some rigorous changes that mostly apply to Easy (now called Casual) and Normal difficulty. From reducing enemy numbers in campaign missions, to adjusting how the AI plays in general, and allowing for more vision range on lower difficulties.[/p][p]I'll be monitoring closely how the difficulty changes are perceived, and I'll adjust accordingly.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Graphics[/b][/p][p]I’ve updated some of the graphics and animations in this build, but the work here is far from finished. You’ll see that the farms now show farm land, and the crops actually grow when created and decay when destroyed. Also, the dirt underneath the farmland stays, affecting the landscape permanently. This is just the start of the graphics changes planned for the game; more will come soon![/p][p][/p][p][b]Change log:[/b]

notes.title: Boons, upgrades & customization
notes.content:
“For this here incredulous feat, a boon is awarded to thee!” 
This patch includes the new boon system to customize your factions, new upgrades, a campaign rework, and various gameplay improvements.

[b]Boons & customization[/b]
Players can now unlock boons when finishing campaign missions or certain achievements. Boons are special upgrades you can select in the menu to enhance certain capabilities of your faction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44916183/cd303269099d69207979bed60ab5b57a124b46d1.png[/img]
Boons vary from economy boosts to hero buffs to troop enhancements and defensive perks. This way, you can customize each faction to play more to your liking.
The current patch includes 10 general boons and 8 faction-specific boons for each faction.  More are coming soon!

[b]Campaign rework[/b]
The campaign received a slight overhaul to make it less linear and give players more freedom to play as they like. There are now faction-specific “intro” missions, while the main set of campaign missions can be played by 2-3 factions each (Ura missions are coming soon).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44916183/379808fa3dfe463317b4ca0a3051e2ed4e12e37b.png[/img]
This includes an all-new campaign mission and a small narrative overhaul regarding the first Fahad mission, which is now set at the start of the current timeline instead of the middle. 
Unfortunately, some previously saved campaign matches will be corrupted. Our apologies for the inconvenience. Any match saved after this patch should work just fine.

[b]Upgrades and conditions[/b]
All factions received various upgrades for their troops to further customize your play-style and provide more options to counter your opponent. Some upgrades use the new conditions, which apply an effect to enemies hit depending on the type of condition; other upgrades change how troops are played, sometimes drastically. 

Conditions are effects that linger on the affected character:
- Bleeding: takes rapid damage over time that increases with intensity the more the character is bleeding.
- Burning: takes damage over time and spawns fires, dealing area damage.
- Poison: takes low damage over a long time. Character can’t be healed for the entire duration.
- Corrosion (used by Wargolems): reduces the character’s armor.
- Chill: slows the character’s movement and attack speed for the duration (up to 50%).
- Stun: the character can’t move, attack, or cast abilities for the duration.

[b]Other features[/b]
- Removed workers automatically targeting faraway structures.
- You can now choose a random faction and hero in battle mode.
- You can choose a campaign mission and equipped boons after each campaign mission.

[b]Bug fixes[/b]
- Fixed an issue where workers with a job couldn’t get selected immediately when troops were selected
- The skip button in the campaign dialogue has been removed since it was confusing for some players. We’re looking into a better option to skip the dialogue for repeated missions.
- The AI now disables the lava-towers on Babalar in battle mode correctly at the start of the match (also in the main menu).
- Golem workers played the wrong sound on dying.

notes.title: First batch of gameplay improvements
notes.content:

notes.title: Counter Clash early access!
notes.content:
Sharpen your blades, light your fires, and ready your muskets, for battle will commence!

Counter Clash Early Access is live! Many thanks to all our supporters for your continued passion and patience.
And for our loyal supporters, there is a 15% early bird discount. Get it now before it goes!

We'll monitor community feedback closely to identify any issues in the game and your thoughts on additional content will help plan releases during Early Access. Features that are popular will be bumped up the priority list. 

Here are some example features that we plan on delivering in the near future:
- Faction customization
- New heroes
- A new campaign featuring the Ura

We look forward to hearing your thoughts.

Happy clashing!

-Bjenssen

notes.title: Throwing cactuses and giving thanks.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44916183/3f5ec31e437fd3538e28896f351a10013153cf58.jpg[/img]

New units join the battle!

Monceaux get the priest, and a fitting new structure:
Church: a structure that heals nearby allies and buffs their attack speed. It can also train priests.
Priest: a support unit that can't attack but heals nearby allies and buffs their attack speed.

Fahad get the Cactus guru at the Nomad Camps level 2: 
Cactus guru: a ranged unit that needles and cactuses that block enemies and deal damage. (Note: The Cactus Guru can only be played against when playing against the Fahad after finishing mission#3 in the campaign. The Fahad faction will be available for play on release early this year.)

Unit updates:
This patch also includes various updates to unit pathfinding and auto-targeting, making it less likely for units to be ambushed while traveling and improving their responsiveness to your input.
There's also a huge update on how enemies use their troops. They now assemble armies just like you that move in formations and attack together. There are still some quirks to be resolved around this new feature, so let me know how this works for you!

Screen resolutions:
You can now switch between fullscreen and windowed mode and adjust the window to your liking, this works for most standard sizes.

Difficulty:
Some missions were too hard to beat for new players. I'd like new players to have a nice time with Easy difficulty and not face too much pushback while providing a complex challenge for more experienced players playing on Hard difficulty.
- Difficulty has been adjusted for the first 3 campaign missions, mainly Easy but also Normal is more forgiving now. This will be continued at further levels, which will be available soon!
- General difficulty has been tweaked for the Battle mode. Easy now plays even more casually, while Insane provides more challenge than before.

As always, let me know what you think, and happy clashing!

notes.title: Spooks, bombard towers and eco upgrades!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44916183/21a908b33cefaca6be92c483d07ece3a4e2e711d.png[/img]

What else would you need for Halloween if not spooky scary skeletons?

For this event some new neutral units have arrived that will stick around much longer!
- Graveyard: spawns skeletons and replaces neutral nomad camps for some maps.
- Raiding Specters: a random event where groups of specters spawn near pumpkins and attack the nearest player. More random events will be available on release.
Graveyards and specters only spawn in the Battle mode for now.

Monceaux received various updates, the other factions will follow later:
- Bombard towers: are a new type of tower for the Monceaux. They have low attack speed and can't shoot from close range, but deal massive penetrating damage!
- Versatile lumber camps: upgrade the lumber camp for more efficiency and the capability of mining rocks, making more room for your farms.
- Watcher farms: upgrade the farm with a tower. Farmers automatically go inside when enemies arrive to bombard them with arrows.

Other updates:
The Fahad will be included in the demo for 1 more week. The Battle game mode is now highlighted to promote players trying them out there. They can only be played in the Battle or Training mode.
An event Icon has been added, more updates and more events are coming soon!

I'm aware of the bug regarding some units not wanting to retreat at times. The next focus is on gameplay experience so this bug, some others, and some additional quality-of-life improvements should be tackled soon.

notes.title: Heroes update
notes.content:
[h1]Heroes join the battle![/h1]

[b]Heroes[/b] are unique characters that can be leveled during the game to unlock [b]powerful abilities[/b].

[previewyoutube=8HrS6K3QpQc;full][/previewyoutube]

Currently [b]two heroes[/b] have been added to the demo, more will follow:

[b]Lieutenant Moss:[/b] A Monceaux [b]brawler[/b] hero who specializes in various weapon combat arts.
- Ability 1: Spear throw, a heavy damage range attack.
- Ability 2: Shield, Moss gains a huge defense boost.
- Ability 3: Mace flurry, a heavy area damage melee attack.

[b]Alyssa the Shaman:[/b] A Fahadian [b]ranger[/b] hero with high mobility and the power of sand.
- Ability 1: Leadership, a movement and attack speed buff for nomads and sand troops around her.
- Ability 2: Piercing shots, Alyssa fires arrows with increased penetration and attack speed.
- Ability 3: Tornado, summons a tornado that redirects enemy projectiles.

During Next Fest the second faction, [b]the Fahad, is available for play[/b], so don't miss it and let me know what you think here or in the discord: https://discord.gg/8bNMBkr7te


This update also includes a ton of bug fixes and gameplay improvements. 
- Various unit improvements, mainly the Dust Devil (Fahad) and the Chariot (Monceaux) are a lot stronger and more player-friendly.
- Various crashes are removed.
- Troops now react better than ever to your commands.
- Big armies no longer form one long line, but can stand next to each other.
- Performance is improved even further.
- Various tips are included in the tip system.
- Improvements to worker management.
- Improved info on troops and buildings through an info system and better descriptions.
- Multiple buildings can be selected at once and buildings of the same type can have units trained simultaneously.

I hope you're having a blast, Cheers!

notes.title: Charriots and free training
notes.content:
[b]Training mode update[/b]
You can now place as many troops as you like for both you and your opponent in the training mode. The level and gold constraints are removed, and only faction restraints remain.

[b]New Monceaux unit: Chariots[/b]
The Monceaux get a new unit at the lvl 3 stables: the Chariot. It's a high-speed unit with powerful crossbow shots, devastating blade cleaves, and an incredibly tanky bulk. 
Just make sure you don't lose the horses!

[previewyoutube=EMgrj3QqS1M;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Various other updates[/b]
This update includes various gameplay improvements for economy management, troop management, and troop responsiveness. Some highlights:
- You can now move the camera to a Control Group by pressing it twice.
- You can now assign or unassign builders through a button on the building.
- Armies have improved unit ordering and targeting.

The campaign has also gone through various improvements, with updated characters and dialogue, and various balance and bug fixes.

notes.title: Economy update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44916183/8fe5a11eee46a85f5b09ee249f6d6101bfa40af0.png[/img]

Clear forests to make room for your farms, or create a trade route across the entire map. Just watch out for any raiders that like a share of the profit!

Try the new economy system of the first faction in the demo now. Other factions will be available on release.

The economy update also includes various visual updates, bug fixes, and gameplay improvements.

notes.title: Demo update: Visual overhaul and quality of life.
notes.content:
[b]New unit visuals[/b]
[list]
[*] Monceaux archer (+upgrade)
[*] Monceaux guard (+upgrade)
[*] Crossbowman
[*] Cavalry
[*] Knights
[*] Firebreather
[*] Sandsurfer
[*] Earthmaster
[/list]

[b]New environment visuals[/b]
[list]
[*] Revised basic environment visuals
[*] New look for map 3 (the siege)
[*] Added day-night cycle for campaign and battle game modes
[/list]

[b]Building visuals[/b]
[list]
[*] Added building destruction vfx
[*] Added fire VFX on damaged buildings
[/list]

[b]UI changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Visual changes
[*] Added short keys (removed WASD controls for moving the camera)
[*] Added control groups (ctrl 1-5 to set, 1-5 to use)
[/list]

[b]FPS improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Refactored GPU processes to run more smoothly
[/list]

[b]Other fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed deselecting or moving units when interacting with UI elements
[*] Fixed deselecting or setting a rallying point with buildings when interacting with UI elements
[*] Changed the resources UI in training mode to match other game modes
[*] You can now move the game view with the mouse
[*] Reworked farm placement
[*] Improved resource visuals
[*] Added unique cursor
[*] Fixed units getting permanently stuck (move them a few times to unstuck)
[/list]
